body.x: Strutt, a new mobility technology startup, has given media and key industry partners an exclusive preview of its flagship product, the STRUTT ev¹, a smart personal vehicle that integrates advanced automotive sensing and robotics to redefine personal mobility. The private event, dubbed “Strutt Day,” served as a significant pre-launch milestone ahead of the ev¹’s official world premiere at CES 2026 in Las Vegas.

The ev¹ has already generated significant industry buzz, having earned the prestigious Red Dot: Luminary 2025—the highest design concept distinction globally—and the CES 2026 Best of Innovation award in the Vehicle Technology & Advanced Mobility category.

At Strutt Day, attendees were introduced to the company's vision by Founder and CEO Tony Hong, who explained that the mission is to bridge the gap between cutting-edge technology and the real, everyday challenges faced by mobility users.

“We started Strutt because we saw a gap between incredible technology and the real problems people face every day,” Hong said. “Strutt Day isn’t just about our product; it’s about showing the world how thoughtful design and intelligent technologies can transform lives.”

Barney Mason, Head of Design, articulated the design philosophy of “Quiet Empowerment,” aiming to create technology that subtly blends into daily life while boosting user confidence and independence. The development process involved extensive user research, guiding every detail from the chassis to the joystick placement, to ensure the design supports dignity and natural movement.
The STRUTT ev¹ is built around two core, proprietary innovations that bring self-driving car technology into personal mobility:

The first innovation is the evSense System, a 360-degree sensing and decision-making system. This system uses a combination of sensors, including LiDAR, cameras, ultrasonic, and Time-of-Flight (ToF). This advanced setup allows for safe, real-world navigation and automatic obstacle avoidance, significantly reducing the need for constant hyper-vigilance.

The second core innovation is the Quad-Drive System, a four-wheel active drive architecture with powerful quad motors. This system ensures smooth, controlled movement across diverse environments, from indoor spaces and carpets to challenging outdoor terrains and inclines, enhancing both safety and performance.

Attendees at the showcase experienced the vehicle’s capabilities firsthand, confirming its goal of addressing the current challenges of complexity, outdated technology, and the social stigma often associated with mobility devices.

The company, incorporated in Singapore and backed by investors including Matter Venture Partners and Vertex Ventures, combines world-leading expertise in advanced sensing and autonomous robotics with a people-centered research approach. The highly anticipated global launch at CES 2026 will unveil final details, including pricing and availability, setting the stage for Strutt to become a major player in the evolving smart mobility sector.
